884: func (s Service) runReviewer(ctx context.Context, m ReviewManifest, c ReviewInput, resumeSession string, onSession func(string)) (out ReviewCoverageResult, sessionID string) {
885: 	out.CoverageID = c.ID
886: 	defer func() {
887: 		if r := recover(); r != nil {
888: 			out.Error = fmt.Sprintf("reviewer panic: %v", r)
889: 		}
890: 	}()
891: 	stagePrompt := renderReviewerPrompt(m, c)
892: 	if resumeSession != "" {
893: 		stagePrompt = "Resume the interrupted review using the refreshed frozen snapshot paths in this request. " + stagePrompt
894: 	}
895: 	prompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, stagePrompt)
896: 	if composeErr != nil {
897: 		out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, composeErr.Error())
898: 		return
899: 	}
900: 	req := s.runtimeRequest(prompt, map[string]string{"project": m.Project, "sprint": m.Sprint, "stage": string(StageReview), "coverage": c.ID, "model_source": m.ModelSource})
901: 	req.WorkDir = m.ReviewerRoot
902: 	req.Model = strings.TrimPrefix(m.Model, req.Provider+"/")
903: 	req.Sandbox = "read_only"
904: 	req.Permissions = "restricted"
905: 	req.RequireCaps = appendUnique(req.RequireCaps, "permissions")
906: 	req.Policy = pruntime.PermissionPolicy{Default: "deny", Tools: map[string]string{"read": "allow", "list": "allow", "search": "allow"}}
907: 	captured := &reviewOutputCapture{}
908: 	req.Validation = s.reviewValidationSpec(m, c, captured)
909: 	if resumeSession != "" {
910: 		req.SessionID, req.SessionAction = resumeSession, "continue"
911: 	}
912: 	previousOnEvent := req.OnEvent
913: 	req.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
914: 		captured.observe(event.Payload)
915: 		if previousOnEvent != nil {
916: 			previousOnEvent(event)
917: 		}
918: 		if event.SessionID != "" {
919: 			if onSession != nil {
920: 				onSession(event.SessionID)
921: 			}
922: 		}
923: 	}
924: 	sp := Sprint{Project: m.Project, Slug: m.Sprint, Path: filepath.Join(s.root, "projects", m.Project, "sprints", m.Sprint)}
925: 	r, err := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageReview, req)
926: 	sessionID = r.SessionID
927: 	if sessionID != "" && onSession != nil {
928: 		onSession(sessionID)
929: 	}
930: 	if r.Permissions.UnsupportedCount > 0 {
931: 		out.Error = "runtime could not enforce review permission policy"
932: 		return
933: 	}
934: 	if ctx.Err() != nil {
935: 		out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, ctx.Err().Error())
936: 		return
937: 	}
938: 	candidate, problems := extractValidatedReviewResult(s.root, m, c.ID, r)
939: 	if err == nil && len(problems) == 0 {
940: 		return candidate, sessionID
941: 	}
942: 	// The production AgentWrap stack already performed its bounded repairs.
943: 	// Runtime implementations without that wrapper retain a small equivalent
944: 	// fallback here so the product boundary remains deterministic in tests and
945: 	// alternate adapters.
946: 	if r.Validation.Configured {
947: 		if len(problems) == 0 && !r.Validation.Passed && len(r.Validation.Details) > 0 {
948: 			problems = append(problems, r.Validation.Details...)
949: 		}
950: 		if len(problems) > 0 {
951: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, strings.Join(problems, "; "))
952: 		} else if err != nil {
953: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())
954: 		}
955: 		return
956: 	}
957: 	if len(problems) == 0 && err != nil {
958: 		problems = []string{safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())}
959: 	}
960: 	for attempt := 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++ {
961: 		repair := req
962: 		repair.Validation = nil
963: 		repair.Prompt, composeErr = composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, buildReviewRepairPrompt(m, c, problems, r.TerminalOutput))
964: 		if composeErr != nil {
965: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, composeErr.Error())
966: 			return
967: 		}
968: 		if attempt == 1 && sessionID != "" {
969: 			repair.SessionID, repair.SessionAction = sessionID, "continue"
970: 		} else {
971: 			repair.SessionID, repair.SessionAction = "", "fresh"
972: 		}
973: 		repaired, repairErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageReview, repair)
974: 		if repaired.SessionID != "" {
975: 			sessionID = repaired.SessionID
976: 			if onSession != nil {
977: 				onSession(sessionID)
978: 			}
979: 		}
980: 		if repaired.Permissions.UnsupportedCount > 0 {
981: 			out.Error = "runtime could not enforce review permission policy during repair"
982: 			return
983: 		}
984: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
985: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, ctx.Err().Error())
986: 			return
987: 		}
988: 		candidate, problems = extractValidatedReviewResult(s.root, m, c.ID, repaired)
989: 		if repairErr == nil && len(problems) == 0 {
990: 			return candidate, sessionID
991: 		}
992: 		if len(problems) == 0 && repairErr != nil {

267: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Review prerequisites", entry.Name(), rel, "missing area reasoning input", safeError(fileErr), "Restore selected area reasoning."))
268: 				continue
269: 			}
270: 			manifest.Contents[rel] = string(data)
271: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, reviewInput("area-"+slugReviewID(entry.Name()), "governed", entry.Name(), rel, string(data)))
272: 		}
273: 	}
274: 	planManifest, planFindings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
275: 	findings = append(findings, planFindings...)
276: 	if len(planFindings) == 0 {
277: 		findings = append(findings, ValidatePlanContent(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan)], planManifest)...)
278: 	}
279: 	runPath := ExecuteRunStateRelPath(sp)
280: 	if data, readErr := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(runPath))); readErr == nil {
281: 		manifest.Contents[runPath] = string(data)
282: 		manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, reviewInput("run-state", "governed", "run-state", runPath, string(data)))
283: 		manifest.ChangedPaths = excludeGovernedReviewPaths(reviewChangedPaths(data), manifest.Inputs)
284: 	} else {
285: 		manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, ReviewInput{ID: "run-state", Kind: "governed", Name: "run-state", Path: runPath, Hash: "missing"})
286: 	}
287: 	if target.Path != "" {
288: 		identity, identityErr := targetRevisionIdentity(target.Path)
289: 		if identityErr != nil {
290: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", "target identity", "target/.identity", "target identity unavailable", identityErr.Error(), "Restore a contained readable target tree."))
291: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, ReviewInput{ID: "target-identity", Kind: "target", Name: "target identity", Path: "target/.identity", Hash: "missing"})
292: 		} else {
293: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, ReviewInput{ID: "target-identity", Kind: "target", Name: "target identity", Path: "target/.identity", Hash: identity})
294: 		}
295: 	}
296: 	resolve := func(selected SelectedItem, section project.CatalogSection, kind, prefix string, reviewer bool) {
297: 		entry, ok := catalogEntry(catalog, section, selected)
298: 		if !ok {
299: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Review manifest", selected.Name, selected.Path, "catalog entry unresolved", "selected entry is not uniquely resolvable", "Fix project-index.md or sprint-index.md."))
300: 			return
301: 		}
302: 		path := entry.Path
303: 		full, pathErr := workspace.ResolveInside(s.root, path)
304: 		if pathErr != nil {
305: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Review manifest", selected.Name, path, "unsafe catalog path", pathErr.Error(), "Use a contained workspace path."))
306: 			return
307: 		}
308: 		data, readErr := os.ReadFile(full)
309: 		if readErr != nil {
310: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, ReviewInput{ID: prefix + "-" + slugReviewID(selected.Name), Kind: kind, Name: selected.Name, Path: path, Hash: "missing"})
311: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Review manifest", selected.Name, path, "unreadable catalog entry", readErr.Error(), "Restore the selected catalog file."))
312: 			return
313: 		}
314: 		id := prefix + "-" + slugReviewID(selected.Name)
315: 		in := reviewInput(id, kind, selected.Name, path, string(data))
316: 		manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, in)
317: 		if reviewer {
318: 			manifest.Coverage = append(manifest.Coverage, in)
319: 		}
320: 		manifest.Contents[path] = string(data)
321: 	}
322: 	for _, selected := range idx.Contracts {
323: 		resolve(selected, project.SectionActiveContractPool, "contract", "contract", true)
324: 	}
325: 	for _, selected := range idx.ReviewProtocols {
326: 		resolve(selected, project.SectionReviewProtocols, "protocol", "protocol", false)
327: 	}
328: 	if unresolvedExecutePlanTasks(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan)], manifest.Contents[runPath], planManifest) {
329: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Plan Execution", "tasks", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "plan tasks are not resolved", "one or more unchecked top-level tasks lack an explicit deferred run-state outcome", "Complete each executable task or defer it with an explicit rationale before review."))
330: 	}
331: 	// The handbook receives an independent reviewer even though it is also a governed input.
332: 	if handbook := findReviewInput(manifest.Inputs, "technical-handbook"); handbook.Path != "" {
333: 		handbook.ID, handbook.Kind, handbook.Name = "handbook", "handbook", "Technical Handbook"
334: 		manifest.Coverage = append(manifest.Coverage, handbook)
335: 	}
336: 	if strings.TrimSpace(manifest.Model) == "" || manifest.Model == "unresolved" {
337: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "review model", "", "missing review model", "no review, plan, or runtime model is configured", "Set planning.review_model or planning.plan_model."))
338: 	}
339: 	for _, command := range reviewVerificationCommands(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan)]) {
340: 		if !strings.Contains(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)], command) {
341: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Verification Evidence", command, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute), "approved verification evidence missing", "execute.md does not record the planned command", "Run the approved command and record its result in execute.md."))
342: 		}
343: 	}
344: 	if run := manifest.Contents[runPath]; run != "" && reviewRunStateIncomplete([]byte(run)) {
345: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Plan Execution", "run-state", runPath, "execute is incomplete", "run state contains non-complete tasks or status", "Complete or safely resolve execute before review."))
346: 	}
347: 	if len(manifest.ChangedPaths) == 0 {
348: 		manifest.ChangedPaths = []string{"(execute evidence did not enumerate changed paths)"}
349: 	} else {
350: 		for _, changed := range manifest.ChangedPaths {
351: 			full := changed
352: 			if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
353: 				full = filepath.Join(manifest.Target, filepath.FromSlash(changed))
354: 			}
355: 			if !inside(manifest.Target, full) {
356: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", changed, changed, "changed path escapes target", "path is outside the approved implementation target", "Use contained execute evidence."))
357: 				continue
358: 			}
359: 			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(full)
360: 			if readErr != nil {
361: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", changed, changed, "changed target input unreadable", readErr.Error(), "Restore the changed path or correct execute evidence."))
362: 				continue
363: 			}
364: 			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(manifest.Target, full)
365: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, reviewInput("target-"+slugReviewID(rel), "target", rel, "target/"+filepath.ToSlash(rel), string(data)))
366: 			manifest.Contents["target/"+filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = string(data)
367: 		}
368: 	}
369: 	sort.Slice(manifest.Coverage, func(i, j int) bool { return manifest.Coverage[i].ID < manifest.Coverage[j].ID })
370: 	sort.Slice(manifest.Inputs, func(i, j int) bool { return manifest.Inputs[i].Path < manifest.Inputs[j].Path })
371: 	manifest.Fingerprint = fingerprintReviewManifest(manifest)
372: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
373: 	return manifest, findings, nil
374: }

404: func (s Service) Review(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req ReviewRequest) (ReviewResult, error) {
405: 	m, findings, err := s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, req)
406: 	result := ReviewResult{Project: m.Project, Sprint: m.Sprint, DryRun: req.DryRun, Fingerprint: m.Fingerprint, Artifact: reviewArtifact(m), Status: ReviewReady, Focused: append([]string(nil), req.Focus...)}
407: 	if err != nil {
408: 		return result, err
409: 	}
410: 	if !req.DryRun && !req.PromptOnly {
411: 		lockedCtx, release, lockErr := s.acquireMutationContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef)
412: 		if lockErr != nil {
413: 			return result, lockErr
414: 		}
415: 		defer release()
416: 		ctx = lockedCtx
417: 	}
418: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
419: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewBlocked, ReviewVerdictBlocked
420: 		for _, f := range findings {
421: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "preflight", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, f.Problem+": "+f.Cause)})
422: 		}
423: 		if !req.DryRun {
424: 			if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); saveErr != nil {
425: 				return result, errors.Join(fmt.Errorf("review prerequisites failed validation"), saveErr)
426: 			}
427: 		}
428: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("review prerequisites failed validation")
429: 	}
430: 	sp, inputs, _, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
431: 	if err != nil {
432: 		return result, err
433: 	}
434: 	m.SharedPrefix, err = s.prepareSharedPromptContext(ctx, sp, inputs, true)
435: 	if err != nil {
436: 		if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
437: 			result.Status = ReviewCancelled
438: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())})
439: 			if !req.DryRun && !req.PromptOnly {
440: 				return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), err)
441: 			}
442: 		}
443: 		return result, err
444: 	}
445: 	result.Prompt, err = composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, renderReviewPreview(m))
446: 	if err != nil {
447: 		return result, err
448: 	}
449: 	if req.DryRun || req.PromptOnly {
450: 		result.Message = "review dry run"
451: 		return result, nil
452: 	}
453: 	if s.runtime == nil {
454: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for review")
455: 	}
456: 	if req.Restart && len(req.Focus) > 0 {
457: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("--restart cannot be combined with focused review")
458: 	}
459: 	result.Status = ReviewRunning
460: 	result.Restarted = req.Restart
461: 	if err := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); err != nil {
462: 		return result, err
463: 	}
464: 	runCoverage, coverage, focusErr := s.reviewCoveragePlan(projectRef, sprintRef, m, req.Focus)
465: 	if focusErr != nil {
466: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewBlocked, ReviewVerdictBlocked
467: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "focus", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, focusErr.Error())})
468: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), focusErr)
469: 	}
470: 	resumeSessions := map[string]string{}
471: 	completed := 0
472: 	if len(req.Focus) == 0 {
473: 		resume, rebased, resumeErr := s.initializeReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef, m, req.Restart)
474: 		if resumeErr != nil {
475: 			result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
476: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "resume-state", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, resumeErr.Error())})
477: 			return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), resumeErr)
478: 		}
479: 		runCoverage, coverage, resumeSessions, completed = reviewResumePlan(s.root, m, resume)
480: 		result.Resumed = !req.Restart && (completed > 0 || len(resumeSessions) > 0)
481: 		result.Reused = completed
482: 		if rebased > 0 {
483: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "resume-rebased", Message: fmt.Sprintf("reused %d validated reviewer result(s) from the prior input fingerprint; incomplete coverage uses the current snapshot", rebased)})
484: 		}
485: 	}
486: 	reviewerRoot, snapshotErr := prepareReviewSnapshot(m)
487: 	if snapshotErr != nil {
488: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
489: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "snapshot", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, snapshotErr.Error())})
490: 		if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); saveErr != nil {
491: 			return result, errors.Join(snapshotErr, saveErr)
492: 		}
493: 		return result, snapshotErr
494: 	}
495: 	m.ReviewerRoot = reviewerRoot
496: 	workers := m.Concurrency
497: 	if workers > len(runCoverage) {
498: 		workers = len(runCoverage)
499: 	}
500: 	if workers < 1 {
501: 		workers = 1
502: 	}
503: 	type item struct {
504: 		index     int
505: 		value     ReviewCoverageResult
506: 		sessionID string
507: 	}
508: 	type sessionItem struct {
509: 		coverageID string
510: 		sessionID  string
511: 	}
512: 	jobs := make(chan int)
513: 	done := make(chan item, len(runCoverage))
514: 	sessions := make(chan sessionItem, max(1, len(runCoverage)*4))
515: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
516: 	for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {
517: 		wg.Add(1)
518: 		go func() {
519: 			defer wg.Done()
520: 			for i := range jobs {
521: 				c := runCoverage[i]
522: 				sessionID := resumeSessions[c.ID]
523: 				lastSessionID := sessionID
524: 				value, finalSessionID := s.runReviewer(ctx, m, c, sessionID, func(id string) {
525: 					if id != "" && id != lastSessionID {
526: 						lastSessionID = id
527: 						sessions <- sessionItem{coverageID: c.ID, sessionID: id}
528: 					}
529: 				})
530: 				done <- item{index: i, value: value, sessionID: finalSessionID}
531: 			}
532: 		}()
533: 	}
534: 	go func() {
535: 		for i := range runCoverage {
536: 			jobs <- i
537: 		}
538: 		close(jobs)
539: 		wg.Wait()
540: 		close(sessions)
541: 		close(done)
542: 	}()
543: 	var progressSaveErr error
544: 	completedSessionIDs := map[string]bool{}
545: 	for done != nil || sessions != nil {
546: 		select {
547: 		case session, ok := <-sessions:
548: 			if !ok {
549: 				sessions = nil
550: 				continue
551: 			}
552: 			if session.sessionID != "" && len(req.Focus) == 0 {
553: 				if saveErr := s.saveReviewResumeSession(projectRef, sprintRef, m.Fingerprint, session.coverageID, session.sessionID); saveErr != nil {
554: 					progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
555: 				}
556: 			}
557: 		case got, ok := <-done:
558: 			if !ok {
559: 				done = nil
560: 				continue
561: 			}
562: 			if got.value.Error == "" && !reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(s.root, m, got.value) {
563: 				got.value.Error = "reviewer result failed schema or citation validation"
564: 			}
565: 			for i := range m.Coverage {
566: 				if m.Coverage[i].ID == got.value.CoverageID {
567: 					coverage[i] = got.value
568: 					break
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 			completed++
572: 			if got.sessionID != "" {
573: 				completedSessionIDs[got.sessionID] = true
574: 			}
575: 			if req.Progress != nil {
576: 				req.Progress(ReviewProgress{Completed: completed, Total: len(coverage), CoverageID: got.value.CoverageID, Message: "reviewer complete"})
577: 			}
578: 			result.Coverage = coverage
579: 			if len(req.Focus) == 0 {
580: 				if saveErr := s.saveReviewResumeResult(projectRef, sprintRef, m.Fingerprint, got.value, got.sessionID); saveErr != nil {
581: 					progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
582: 				}
583: 			}
584: 			if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage)); saveErr != nil {
585: 				progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
586: 			}
587: 		}
588: 	}
589: 	result.Coverage = coverage
590: 	validatedFindings, validationDiagnostics, validatedVerdict := validateReviewCoverage(s.root, m, coverage)
591: 	result.Findings = validatedFindings
592: 	result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, validationDiagnostics...)
593: 	result.Verdict = validatedVerdict
594: 	if progressSaveErr != nil {
595: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
596: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "state-write-failed", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, progressSaveErr.Error())})
597: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), progressSaveErr)
598: 	}
599: 	if ctx.Err() != nil {
600: 		result.Status = ReviewCancelled
601: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: ctx.Err().Error()})
602: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), ctx.Err())
603: 	}
604: 	if result.Verdict == ReviewVerdictBlocked {
605: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
606: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), fmt.Errorf("review failed to produce complete valid coverage"))
607: 	}
608: 	current, currentFindings, currentErr := s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, req)
609: 	if currentErr != nil || len(currentFindings) > 0 || current.Fingerprint != m.Fingerprint {
610: 		for _, message := range reviewManifestChanges(m, current, currentFindings, currentErr) {
611: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "inputs-changed", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, message)})
612: 		}
613: 	}
614: 	result.Status = ReviewCompleted
615: 	content := RenderReviewMarkdown(m, result)
616: 	if vf := ValidateReviewContent(content, m); len(vf) > 0 {
617: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
618: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "artifact-invalid", Message: vf[0].Problem})
619: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), fmt.Errorf("generated review.md failed validation"))
620: 	}
621: 	path, _ := ArtifactPath(s.root, sp, StageReview)
622: 	if err := atomicWriteReview(path, []byte(content)); err != nil {
623: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
624: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "write-failed", Message: safeError(err)})
625: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), err)
626: 	}
627: 	now := s.now().UTC()
628: 	result.Message = "review complete"
629: 	result.Artifact = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageReview)
630: 	if err := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage)); err != nil {
631: 		return result, err
632: 	}
633: 	publications, publishErr := s.publishReviewStage(ctx, sp)
634: 	result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
635: 	if publishErr != nil {
636: 		return result, publishErr
637: 	}
638: 	_ = os.RemoveAll(reviewerRoot)
639: 	_ = now
640: 	if result.Verdict == ReviewFail {
641: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("review completed with failing verdict")
642: 	}
643: 	for sessionID := range completedSessionIDs {
644: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSession(ctx, sessionID)
645: 	}
646: 	return result, nil
647: }

651: 		return result, errors.Join(cause, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal review state: %w", saveErr))
652: 	}
653: 	return result, cause

656: func (s Service) reviewCoveragePlan(projectRef, sprintRef string, m ReviewManifest, focus []string) ([]ReviewInput, []ReviewCoverageResult, error) {
657: 	coverage := make([]ReviewCoverageResult, len(m.Coverage))
658: 	if len(focus) == 0 {
659: 		return m.Coverage, coverage, nil
660: 	}
661: 	wanted := map[string]bool{}
662: 	for _, raw := range focus {
663: 		for _, id := range strings.Split(raw, ",") {
664: 			id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
665: 			if id != "" {
666: 				wanted[id] = true
667: 			}
668: 		}
669: 	}
670: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, Sprint{Project: m.Project, Slug: m.Sprint, Path: filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(m.SprintRoot))})
671: 	if err != nil || state.Review == nil || state.Review.LastComplete == nil {
672: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review requires a previous complete review with retained coverage")
673: 	}
674: 	previous := state.Review.LastComplete
675: 	if previous.InputFingerprint != m.Fingerprint {
676: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review cannot retain coverage from a different input fingerprint")
677: 	}
678: 	retained := map[string]ReviewCoverageResult{}
679: 	for _, item := range previous.Coverage {
680: 		retained[item.CoverageID] = item
681: 	}
682: 	var run []ReviewInput
683: 	for i, item := range m.Coverage {
684: 		if wanted[item.ID] {
685: 			run = append(run, item)
686: 			delete(wanted, item.ID)
687: 			continue
688: 		}
689: 		prior, ok := retained[item.ID]
690: 		if !ok || prior.Error != "" {
691: 			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review lacks valid retained coverage %q", item.ID)
692: 		}
693: 		coverage[i] = prior
694: 	}
695: 	if len(wanted) > 0 {
696: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review names unknown coverage")
697: 	}
698: 	if len(run) == 0 {
699: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review requires at least one coverage id")
700: 	}
701: 	return run, coverage, nil
702: }

704: func (s Service) initializeReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef string, m ReviewManifest, restart bool) (ReviewResumeState, int, error) {
705: 	sp, _, _, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
706: 	if err != nil {
707: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
708: 	}
709: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, sp)
710: 	if err != nil {
711: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
712: 	}
713: 	if state.Review == nil || state.Review.ActiveAttempt == nil {
714: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("review attempt state is unavailable")
715: 	}
716: 	current := state.Review.Resume
717: 	rebased := 0
718: 	if restart || !reviewResumeCompatible(current, m) {
719: 		checkpoints := make([]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint, 0, len(m.Coverage))
720: 		now := s.now().UTC()
721: 		prior := map[string]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{}
722: 		if !restart && reviewResumeShapeCompatible(current, m) {
723: 			for _, checkpoint := range current.Coverage {
724: 				prior[checkpoint.CoverageID] = checkpoint
725: 			}
726: 		}
727: 		for _, item := range m.Coverage {
728: 			checkpoint := ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{CoverageID: item.ID, Status: AttemptPending, UpdatedAt: now}
729: 			if previous, ok := prior[item.ID]; ok && previous.Status == AttemptCompleted && previous.Result != nil && reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(s.root, m, *previous.Result) {
730: 				checkpoint.Status = AttemptCompleted
731: 				checkpoint.Result = previous.Result
732: 				rebased++
733: 			}
734: 			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, checkpoint)
735: 		}
736: 		current = &ReviewResumeState{
737: 			AttemptID:        state.Review.ActiveAttempt.ID,
738: 			InputFingerprint: m.Fingerprint,
739: 			Model:            m.Model,
740: 			UpdatedAt:        now,
741: 			Coverage:         checkpoints,
742: 		}
743: 	} else {
744: 		current.AttemptID = state.Review.ActiveAttempt.ID
745: 		current.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
746: 	}
747: 	state.Review.Resume = current
748: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
749: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
750: 	}
751: 	return *current, rebased, nil
752: }

754: func reviewResumeCompatible(state *ReviewResumeState, m ReviewManifest) bool {
755: 	return state != nil && state.InputFingerprint == m.Fingerprint && reviewResumeShapeCompatible(state, m)
756: }
757: 
758: func reviewResumeShapeCompatible(state *ReviewResumeState, m ReviewManifest) bool {
759: 	if state == nil || state.Model != m.Model || len(state.Coverage) != len(m.Coverage) {
760: 		return false
761: 	}
762: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
763: 	for _, item := range state.Coverage {
764: 		seen[item.CoverageID] = true
765: 	}
766: 	for _, item := range m.Coverage {
767: 		if !seen[item.ID] {
768: 			return false
769: 		}
770: 	}
771: 	return true
772: }

774: func reviewResumePlan(root string, m ReviewManifest, state ReviewResumeState) ([]ReviewInput, []ReviewCoverageResult, map[string]string, int) {
775: 	checkpoints := map[string]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{}
776: 	for _, item := range state.Coverage {
777: 		checkpoints[item.CoverageID] = item
778: 	}
779: 	coverage := make([]ReviewCoverageResult, len(m.Coverage))
780: 	sessions := map[string]string{}
781: 	run := make([]ReviewInput, 0, len(m.Coverage))
782: 	completed := 0
783: 	for i, item := range m.Coverage {
784: 		checkpoint := checkpoints[item.ID]
785: 		if checkpoint.Status == AttemptCompleted && checkpoint.Result != nil && reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(root, m, *checkpoint.Result) {
786: 			coverage[i] = *checkpoint.Result
787: 			completed++
788: 			continue
789: 		}
790: 		if checkpoint.SessionID != "" && state.InputFingerprint == m.Fingerprint {
791: 			sessions[item.ID] = checkpoint.SessionID
792: 		}
793: 		run = append(run, item)
794: 	}
795: 	return run, coverage, sessions, completed
796: }

798: func reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(root string, m ReviewManifest, result ReviewCoverageResult) bool {
799: 	if result.Error != "" {
800: 		return false
801: 	}
802: 	single := m
803: 	single.Coverage = []ReviewInput{{ID: result.CoverageID}}
804: 	_, diagnostics, _ := validateReviewCoverage(root, single, []ReviewCoverageResult{result})
805: 	return len(diagnostics) == 0
806: }

808: func (s Service) saveReviewResumeSession(projectRef, sprintRef, fingerprint, coverageID, sessionID string) error {
809: 	return s.updateReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef, fingerprint, coverageID, func(checkpoint *ReviewCoverageCheckpoint, now time.Time) {
810: 		// Session events and completed results arrive on separate channels. A
811: 		// buffered session event may therefore be persisted after the terminal
812: 		// result; never let that late event restore a cleared session or regress a
813: 		// terminal checkpoint to running.
814: 		if checkpoint.Status == AttemptCompleted || checkpoint.Status == AttemptFailed {
815: 			return
816: 		}
817: 		checkpoint.SessionID = sessionID
818: 		checkpoint.Status = AttemptRunning
819: 		checkpoint.UpdatedAt = now
820: 	})
821: }
822: 
823: func (s Service) saveReviewResumeResult(projectRef, sprintRef, fingerprint string, result ReviewCoverageResult, sessionID string) error {
824: 	return s.updateReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef, fingerprint, result.CoverageID, func(checkpoint *ReviewCoverageCheckpoint, now time.Time) {
825: 		checkpoint.UpdatedAt = now
826: 		if result.Error == "" {
827: 			checkpoint.SessionID = ""
828: 			checkpoint.Status = AttemptCompleted
829: 			copy := result
830: 			checkpoint.Result = &copy
831: 		} else {
832: 			checkpoint.SessionID = sessionID
833: 			checkpoint.Status = AttemptFailed
834: 			checkpoint.Result = nil
835: 		}
836: 	})
837: }

839: func (s Service) updateReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef, fingerprint, coverageID string, update func(*ReviewCoverageCheckpoint, time.Time)) error {
840: 	sp, _, _, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
841: 	if err != nil {
842: 		return err
843: 	}
844: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, sp)
845: 	if err != nil {
846: 		return err
847: 	}
848: 	if state.Review == nil || state.Review.Resume == nil || state.Review.Resume.InputFingerprint != fingerprint {
849: 		return fmt.Errorf("review resume checkpoint no longer matches active inputs")
850: 	}
851: 	now := s.now().UTC()
852: 	if state.Review.ActiveAttempt != nil {
853: 		state.Review.ActiveAttempt.HeartbeatAt = now
854: 		state.Review.ActiveAttempt.OwnerPID = os.Getpid()
855: 	}
856: 	for i := range state.Review.Resume.Coverage {
857: 		if state.Review.Resume.Coverage[i].CoverageID == coverageID {
858: 			update(&state.Review.Resume.Coverage[i], now)
859: 			state.Review.Resume.UpdatedAt = now
860: 			return SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, state)
861: 		}
862: 	}
863: 	return fmt.Errorf("review resume checkpoint missing coverage %q", coverageID)
864: }

884: func (s Service) runReviewer(ctx context.Context, m ReviewManifest, c ReviewInput, resumeSession string, onSession func(string)) (out ReviewCoverageResult, sessionID string) {
885: 	out.CoverageID = c.ID
886: 	defer func() {
887: 		if r := recover(); r != nil {
888: 			out.Error = fmt.Sprintf("reviewer panic: %v", r)
889: 		}
890: 	}()
891: 	stagePrompt := renderReviewerPrompt(m, c)
892: 	if resumeSession != "" {
893: 		stagePrompt = "Resume the interrupted review using the refreshed frozen snapshot paths in this request. " + stagePrompt
894: 	}
895: 	prompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, stagePrompt)
896: 	if composeErr != nil {
897: 		out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, composeErr.Error())
898: 		return
899: 	}
900: 	req := s.runtimeRequest(prompt, map[string]string{"project": m.Project, "sprint": m.Sprint, "stage": string(StageReview), "coverage": c.ID, "model_source": m.ModelSource})
901: 	req.WorkDir = m.ReviewerRoot
902: 	req.Model = strings.TrimPrefix(m.Model, req.Provider+"/")
903: 	req.Sandbox = "read_only"
904: 	req.Permissions = "restricted"
905: 	req.RequireCaps = appendUnique(req.RequireCaps, "permissions")
906: 	req.Policy = pruntime.PermissionPolicy{Default: "deny", Tools: map[string]string{"read": "allow", "list": "allow", "search": "allow"}}
907: 	captured := &reviewOutputCapture{}
908: 	req.Validation = s.reviewValidationSpec(m, c, captured)
909: 	if resumeSession != "" {
910: 		req.SessionID, req.SessionAction = resumeSession, "continue"
911: 	}
912: 	previousOnEvent := req.OnEvent
913: 	req.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
914: 		captured.observe(event.Payload)
915: 		if previousOnEvent != nil {
916: 			previousOnEvent(event)
917: 		}
918: 		if event.SessionID != "" {
919: 			if onSession != nil {
920: 				onSession(event.SessionID)
921: 			}
922: 		}
923: 	}
924: 	sp := Sprint{Project: m.Project, Slug: m.Sprint, Path: filepath.Join(s.root, "projects", m.Project, "sprints", m.Sprint)}
925: 	r, err := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageReview, req)
926: 	sessionID = r.SessionID
927: 	if sessionID != "" && onSession != nil {
928: 		onSession(sessionID)
929: 	}
930: 	if r.Permissions.UnsupportedCount > 0 {
931: 		out.Error = "runtime could not enforce review permission policy"
932: 		return
933: 	}
934: 	if ctx.Err() != nil {
935: 		out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, ctx.Err().Error())
936: 		return
937: 	}
938: 	candidate, problems := extractValidatedReviewResult(s.root, m, c.ID, r)
939: 	if err == nil && len(problems) == 0 {
940: 		return candidate, sessionID
941: 	}
942: 	// The production AgentWrap stack already performed its bounded repairs.
943: 	// Runtime implementations without that wrapper retain a small equivalent
944: 	// fallback here so the product boundary remains deterministic in tests and
945: 	// alternate adapters.
946: 	if r.Validation.Configured {
947: 		if len(problems) == 0 && !r.Validation.Passed && len(r.Validation.Details) > 0 {
948: 			problems = append(problems, r.Validation.Details...)
949: 		}
950: 		if len(problems) > 0 {
951: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, strings.Join(problems, "; "))
952: 		} else if err != nil {
953: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())
954: 		}
955: 		return
956: 	}
957: 	if len(problems) == 0 && err != nil {
958: 		problems = []string{safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())}
959: 	}
960: 	for attempt := 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++ {
961: 		repair := req
962: 		repair.Validation = nil
963: 		repair.Prompt, composeErr = composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, buildReviewRepairPrompt(m, c, problems, r.TerminalOutput))
964: 		if composeErr != nil {
965: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, composeErr.Error())
966: 			return
967: 		}
968: 		if attempt == 1 && sessionID != "" {
969: 			repair.SessionID, repair.SessionAction = sessionID, "continue"
970: 		} else {
971: 			repair.SessionID, repair.SessionAction = "", "fresh"
972: 		}
973: 		repaired, repairErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageReview, repair)
974: 		if repaired.SessionID != "" {
975: 			sessionID = repaired.SessionID
976: 			if onSession != nil {
977: 				onSession(sessionID)
978: 			}
979: 		}
980: 		if repaired.Permissions.UnsupportedCount > 0 {
981: 			out.Error = "runtime could not enforce review permission policy during repair"
982: 			return
983: 		}
984: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
985: 			out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, ctx.Err().Error())
986: 			return
987: 		}
988: 		candidate, problems = extractValidatedReviewResult(s.root, m, c.ID, repaired)
989: 		if repairErr == nil && len(problems) == 0 {
990: 			return candidate, sessionID
991: 		}
992: 		if len(problems) == 0 && repairErr != nil {
993: 			problems = []string{safeReviewText(s.root, repairErr.Error())}
994: 		}
995: 	}
996: 	out.Error = safeReviewText(s.root, "structured review result remained invalid after bounded repair: "+strings.Join(problems, "; "))
997: 	return
998: }

1000: func validateReviewCoverage(root string, m ReviewManifest, results []ReviewCoverageResult) ([]ReviewFinding, []ReviewDiagnostic, ReviewVerdict) {
1001: 	var findings []ReviewFinding
1002: 	var diagnostics []ReviewDiagnostic
1003: 	coverage := map[string]bool{}
1004: 	findingIDs := map[string]string{}
1005: 	for i, r := range results {
1006: 		expectedID := r.CoverageID
1007: 		if i < len(m.Coverage) {
1008: 			expectedID = m.Coverage[i].ID
1009: 		}
1010: 		if r.Error != "" {
1011: 			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "reviewer-failed", CoverageID: expectedID, Message: r.Error})
1012: 			continue
1013: 		}
1014: 		normalizeReviewResultForManifest(m, &r)
1015: 		problems := reviewResultProblems(root, m, expectedID, r)
1016: 		if len(problems) > 0 {
1017: 			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "invalid-result", CoverageID: expectedID, Message: safeReviewText(root, strings.Join(problems, "; "))})
1018: 			continue
1019: 		}
1020: 		coverage[r.CoverageID] = true
1021: 		for _, f := range r.Findings {
1022: 			if priorCoverage, duplicate := findingIDs[f.ID]; duplicate {
1023: 				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "duplicate-finding-id", CoverageID: r.CoverageID, Message: fmt.Sprintf("finding id %q already emitted by %s", f.ID, priorCoverage)})
1024: 				continue
1025: 			}
1026: 			findingIDs[f.ID] = r.CoverageID
1027: 			findings = append(findings, f)
1028: 		}
1029: 	}
1030: 	for _, c := range m.Coverage {
1031: 		if !coverage[c.ID] {
1032: 			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "missing-coverage", CoverageID: c.ID, Message: "required reviewer result missing"})
1033: 		}
1034: 	}
1035: 	sort.Slice(findings, func(i, j int) bool {
1036: 		if findings[i].Severity != findings[j].Severity {
1037: 			return findings[i].Severity < findings[j].Severity
1038: 		}
1039: 		return findings[i].ID < findings[j].ID
1040: 	})
1041: 	if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
1042: 		return findings, diagnostics, ReviewVerdictBlocked
1043: 	}
1044: 	verdict := ReviewPass
1045: 	for _, f := range findings {
1046: 		if !reviewApplicable(f.Applicability) {
1047: 			continue
1048: 		}
1049: 		if f.Severity == "high" || f.Severity == "blocker" {
1050: 			verdict = ReviewFail
1051: 			break
1052: 		}
1053: 		verdict = ReviewPassWithFindings
1054: 	}
1055: 	return findings, diagnostics, verdict
1056: }

1058: func RenderReviewMarkdown(m ReviewManifest, r ReviewResult) string {
1059: 	var b strings.Builder
1060: 	fmt.Fprintln(&b, "# Sprint Review")
1061: 	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\nReview status: `%s`\nVerdict: `%s`\nInput fingerprint: `%s`\nModel: `%s`\nModel source: `%s`\nTarget: `%s`\n", r.Status, r.Verdict, m.Fingerprint, m.Model, m.ModelSource, m.Target)
1062: 	sections := []string{"Review Context", "Input Fingerprint And Scope", "Decision Conformance", "Plan Execution", "Verification Evidence", "Contract Conformance", "Technical Handbook Conformance", "Applicability And Deferred Scope", "Findings", "Deviations", "Final Assessment"}
1063: 	for _, section := range sections {
1064: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n## %s\n\n", section)
1065: 		switch section {
1066: 		case "Review Context":
1067: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Project `%s`, sprint `%s`; automated product-owned review.\n", m.Project, m.Sprint)
1068: 		case "Input Fingerprint And Scope":
1069: 			for _, in := range m.Inputs {
1070: 				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` `%s`\n", in.Path, in.Hash)
1071: 			}
1072: 			fmt.Fprintln(&b, "- Changed paths:")
1073: 			for _, p := range m.ChangedPaths {
1074: 				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - `%s`\n", p)
1075: 			}
1076: 		case "Contract Conformance", "Technical Handbook Conformance", "Applicability And Deferred Scope":
1077: 			for _, c := range r.Coverage {
1078: 				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s: %s\n", c.CoverageID, firstNonEmptyString(c.Applicability, "invalid"), firstNonEmptyString(c.Summary, c.Error, "no summary"))
1079: 			}
1080: 		case "Findings":
1081: 			if len(r.Findings) == 0 {
1082: 				fmt.Fprintln(&b, "No applicable findings.")
1083: 			} else {
1084: 				for _, f := range r.Findings {
1085: 					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- [%s] `%s` %s — %s\n", f.Severity, f.ID, f.Title, f.Detail)
1086: 					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - action: %s\n", f.Action)
1087: 					for _, c := range f.Citations {
1088: 						fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - citation: `%s:%d-%d`\n", c.Path, c.StartLine, c.EndLine)
1089: 					}
1090: 				}
1091: 			}
1092: 		case "Deviations":
1093: 			if len(r.Diagnostics) == 0 {
1094: 				fmt.Fprintln(&b, "None.")
1095: 			} else {
1096: 				for _, d := range r.Diagnostics {
1097: 					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` %s\n", d.Code, d.Message)
1098: 				}
1099: 			}
1100: 		case "Final Assessment":
1101: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Deterministic verdict: `%s`.\n", r.Verdict)
1102: 		default:
1103: 			fmt.Fprintln(&b, "Covered by the frozen manifest, deterministic checks, and cited reviewer evidence above.")
1104: 		}
1105: 	}
1106: 	return b.String()
1107: }

1109: func ValidateReviewContent(content string, m ReviewManifest) []ValidationFinding {
1110: 	var out []ValidationFinding
1111: 	if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" || containsPlaceholder(content) {
1112: 		out = append(out, finding("review.md", "content", reviewArtifact(m), "empty or placeholder review", "canonical review must contain complete rendered evidence", "Rerun review."))
1113: 	}
1114: 	for _, h := range []string{"Review Context", "Input Fingerprint And Scope", "Decision Conformance", "Plan Execution", "Verification Evidence", "Contract Conformance", "Technical Handbook Conformance", "Applicability And Deferred Scope", "Findings", "Deviations", "Final Assessment"} {
1115: 		if !markdownHeadingPresent(content, h) {
1116: 			out = append(out, finding("review.md", h, reviewArtifact(m), "missing required section", "section was not found", "Regenerate review.md."))
1117: 		}
1118: 	}
1119: 	if !strings.Contains(content, "Input fingerprint: `"+m.Fingerprint+"`") {
1120: 		out = append(out, finding("review.md", "fingerprint", reviewArtifact(m), "stale or missing fingerprint", "artifact does not match current governed inputs", "Rerun review."))
1121: 	}
1122: 	validVerdict := false
1123: 	for _, v := range []ReviewVerdict{ReviewPass, ReviewPassWithFindings, ReviewFail} {
1124: 		if strings.Contains(content, "Verdict: `"+string(v)+"`") {
1125: 			validVerdict = true
1126: 		}
1127: 	}
1128: 	if !validVerdict {
1129: 		out = append(out, finding("review.md", "verdict", reviewArtifact(m), "missing valid verdict", "verdict is absent or unsupported", "Rerun review."))
1130: 	}
1131: 	for _, coverage := range m.Coverage {
1132: 		if !strings.Contains(content, "`"+coverage.ID+"`") {
1133: 			out = append(out, finding("review.md", coverage.ID, reviewArtifact(m), "missing reviewer coverage", "required coverage id is absent", "Rerun review."))
1134: 		}
1135: 	}
1136: 	return out
1137: }

1139: func validateReviewStageState(root string, sp Sprint, state ReviewStageState, path string) error {
1140: 	if state.Path != ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageReview) {
1141: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: review path mismatch", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
1142: 	}
1143: 	switch state.Status {
1144: 	case ReviewReady, ReviewRunning, ReviewCompleted, ReviewFailed, ReviewCancelled, ReviewBlocked:
1145: 	default:
1146: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsupported review status %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Status)
1147: 	}
1148: 	if strings.ContainsAny(state.Fingerprint, "\x00\r\n") || state.Completed < 0 || state.Total < 0 || state.Completed > state.Total {
1149: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid review state", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
1150: 	}
1151: 	if state.Verdict != "" && state.Verdict != ReviewPass && state.Verdict != ReviewPassWithFindings && state.Verdict != ReviewFail && state.Verdict != ReviewVerdictBlocked {
1152: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsupported review verdict %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Verdict)
1153: 	}
1154: 	if state.ProvisionalVerdict != "" && state.ProvisionalVerdict != ReviewPass && state.ProvisionalVerdict != ReviewPassWithFindings && state.ProvisionalVerdict != ReviewFail {
1155: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsupported provisional review verdict %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.ProvisionalVerdict)
1156: 	}
1157: 	if err := validateAttempt(state.ActiveAttempt, true); err != nil {
1158: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: review active attempt: %v", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, err)
1159: 	}
1160: 	if err := validateAttempt(state.LastAttempt, false); err != nil {
1161: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: review last attempt: %v", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, err)
1162: 	}
1163: 	if state.Resume != nil {
1164: 		resume := state.Resume
1165: 		if resume.AttemptID == "" || resume.InputFingerprint == "" || resume.Model == "" || resume.UpdatedAt.IsZero() || len(resume.Coverage) == 0 {
1166: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid review resume state", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
1167: 		}
1168: 		if strings.ContainsAny(resume.AttemptID+resume.InputFingerprint+resume.Model, "\x00\r\n") {

Now I have the two primary files. Let me analyze with the review lens: **Failure/concurrency: cancellation, restart, partial progress, retry, idempotency, races, liveness, resource ownership, and unknown outcomes.**

Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **Worker pool / collector loop (Review lines 512-588)**:
   - `jobs := make(chan int)` unbuffered. Workers `for i := range jobs`. Feeder goroutine sends all jobs then closes. 
   - **Cancellation**: If ctx is cancelled mid-fan-out, workers keep pulling jobs and calling runReviewer. runReviewer checks ctx.Err() after startSprintRuntime... but does it check ctx before starting? 90: // Flow owns the ordered sprint state machine. Surfaces map requests and render
91: // this result; they do not schedule stages or duplicate verification policy.
92: func (s Service) Flow(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req FlowRequest) (FlowResult, error) {
93: 	stages, err := flowStages(req.To)
94: 	if err != nil {
95: 		return FlowResult{}, err
96: 	}
97: 	if req.DryRun {
98: 		if req.To == StageReview || req.To == StageSmoke {
99: 			verified, verifyErr := s.Verify(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, VerifyRequest{To: req.To, DryRun: true, Review: req.Review, Smoke: req.Smoke, Progress: req.Progress})
100: 			message := "verification dry run"
101: 			if verified.ReviewResult != nil {
102: 				message = firstNonEmptyString(verified.ReviewResult.Prompt, verified.ReviewResult.Message, message)
103: 			}
104: 			return FlowResult{Project: verified.Project, Sprint: verified.Sprint, To: req.To, DryRun: true, Message: message}, verifyErr
105: 		}
106: 		stages = []PlanningStage{req.To}
107: 	} else {
108: 		// A non-dry flow is the materialization entrypoint for a roadmap sprint.
109: 		// Create its safe skeleton before acquiring the sprint-scoped mutation
110: 		// lease; lease resolution deliberately accepts existing sprints only.
111: 		sp, _, _, resolveErr := s.resolveSprintForRequirements(projectRef, sprintRef, true)
112: 		if resolveErr != nil {
113: 			return FlowResult{}, resolveErr
114: 		}
115: 		sprintRef = sp.Slug
116: 		var release func()
117: 		ctx, release, err = s.acquireMutationContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef)
118: 		if err != nil {
119: 			return FlowResult{}, err
120: 		}
121: 		defer release()
122: 	}
123: 	var result FlowResult
124: 	for _, stage := range stages {
125: 		emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "checking", Message: "checking prerequisites and existing artifact"})
126: 		stageReq := FlowRequest{To: stage, DryRun: req.DryRun, ModelOverride: req.ModelOverride, VariantOverride: req.VariantOverride}
127: 		if !req.DryRun {
128: 			valid, validateErr := s.flowStageAlreadyValid(projectRef, sprintRef, stage)
129: 			if validateErr != nil {
130: 				return FlowResult{}, validateErr
131: 			}
132: 			if valid {
133: 				if stage == StageCodeContext {
134: 					sp, inputs, _, resolveErr := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
135: 					if resolveErr != nil {
136: 						return FlowResult{}, resolveErr
137: 					}
138: 					if _, findings := s.resolveSprintTarget(sp, inputs.ProjectIndex, true); len(findings) > 0 {
139: 						return FlowResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, To: stage, Findings: findings}, fmt.Errorf("code-context sprint workspace creation failed")
140: 					}
141: 				}
142: 				if stage != StageExecute {
143: 					if sp, _, _, resolveErr := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef); resolveErr == nil {
144: 						_ = clearPlanningStageSession(sp, stage)
145: 					}
146: 				}
147: 				result = FlowResult{Project: projectRef, Sprint: sprintRef, To: stage, Message: string(stage) + " already complete"}
148: 				if stage != StageExecute {
149: 					publications, publishErr := s.publishPlanningStage(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, stage)
150: 					result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
151: 					if publishErr != nil {
152: 						emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "publish-failed", Message: publishErr.Error()})
153: 						return result, publishErr
154: 					}
155: 				}
156: 				emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "skipped", Message: "already complete"})
157: 				continue
158: 			}
159: 			emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "running", Message: "starting runtime-backed stage"})
160: 		}
161: 		var stageErr error
162: 		result, stageErr = s.withStageOverrides(req.StageOverrides).runFlowStage(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, stageReq)
163: 		if stageErr != nil {
164: 			emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "failed", Message: "stage failed; inspect validation findings and durable state"})
165: 			return result, stageErr
166: 		}
167: 		if !req.DryRun && stage != StageExecute {
168: 			emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "publishing", Message: "committing completed stage changes"})
169: 			publications, publishErr := s.publishPlanningStage(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, stage)
170: 			result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
171: 			if publishErr != nil {
172: 				emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "publish-failed", Message: publishErr.Error()})
173: 				return result, publishErr
174: 			}
175: 		}
176: 		emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: stage, State: "complete", Message: firstNonEmptyString(result.Message, "stage complete")})
177: 	}
178: 	if req.To == StageReview || req.To == StageSmoke {
179: 		verified, verifyErr := s.Verify(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, VerifyRequest{To: req.To, Review: req.Review, Smoke: req.Smoke, Progress: req.Progress})
180: 		message := fmt.Sprintf("verification assessment=%s next=%s", verified.Verification.Assessment, verified.Verification.NextAction)
181: 		return FlowResult{Project: verified.Project, Sprint: verified.Sprint, To: req.To, Message: message}, verifyErr
182: 	}
183: 	result.To = req.To
184: 	return result, nil
185: }

189: func (s Service) FlowStage(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req FlowRequest) (FlowResult, error) {
190: 	if err := validatePlanningStageTarget(req.To); err != nil {
191: 		return FlowResult{}, err
192: 	}
193: 	if !req.DryRun {
194: 		sp, _, _, resolveErr := s.resolveSprintForRequirements(projectRef, sprintRef, true)
195: 		if resolveErr != nil {
196: 			return FlowResult{}, resolveErr
197: 		}
198: 		sprintRef = sp.Slug
199: 		var release func()
200: 		var err error
201: 		ctx, release, err = s.acquireMutationContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef)
202: 		if err != nil {
203: 			return FlowResult{}, err
204: 		}
205: 		defer release()
206: 	}
207: 	emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: req.To, State: "running", Message: "running selected stage only"})
208: 	result, err := s.withStageOverrides(req.StageOverrides).runFlowStage(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)
209: 	if err != nil {
210: 		emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: req.To, State: "failed", Message: "stage failed; inspect validation findings and durable state"})
211: 		return result, err
212: 	}
213: 	if !req.DryRun {
214: 		emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: req.To, State: "publishing", Message: "committing completed stage changes"})
215: 		publications, publishErr := s.publishPlanningStage(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req.To)
216: 		result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
217: 		if publishErr != nil {
218: 			emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: req.To, State: "publish-failed", Message: publishErr.Error()})
219: 			return result, publishErr
220: 		}
221: 	}
222: 	emitFlow(req.Progress, FlowProgress{Stage: req.To, State: "complete", Message: firstNonEmptyString(result.Message, "stage complete")})
223: 	return result, nil
224: }

226: func (s Service) runFlowStage(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req FlowRequest) (FlowResult, error) {
227: 	switch req.To {
228: 	case StageRequirements:
229: 		return s.FlowRequirements(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)
230: 	case StageCodeContext:
231: 		return s.FlowCodeContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)
232: 	case StageSprintIndex:
233: 		return s.FlowSprintIndex(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)
234: 	case StageTechnicalHandbook:
235: 		return s.FlowTechnicalHandbook(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)

237: 		return s.FlowReasoning(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, req)
238: 	case StagePlan:

240: 	case StageExecute:
241: 		execute, err := s.Execute(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef, ExecuteRequest{DryRun: req.DryRun, Resume: true})
242: 		return FlowResult{Project: execute.Project, Sprint: execute.Sprint, To: StageExecute, DryRun: execute.DryRun, Message: firstNonEmptyString(execute.Prompt, execute.Message), Findings: execute.Findings}, err
243: 	default:
244: 		return FlowResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported flow stage %q", req.To)
245: 	}

83: func isPreCodeContextStages(stages []StageState) bool {
84: 	if len(stages) != len(PlanningStages())-1 {

96: func interpretPreCodeContextStages(sp Sprint, stages []StageState) []StageState {
97: 	out := make([]StageState, 0, len(stages)+1)
98: 	out = append(out, stages[0])
99: 	inserted := StageState{Stage: StageCodeContext, Status: StatusMissing, Path: ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageCodeContext)}
100: 	if stages[0].Status == StatusComplete {
101: 		inserted.Status = StatusReady
102: 		for _, later := range stages[1:] {

105: 				inserted.LastRunAt = stages[0].LastRunAt

109: 	}

294: func ValidateFlowState(root string, s Sprint, state FlowState, path string) error {
295: 	if state.SchemaVersion == 0 {
296: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing schemaVersion", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
297: 	}
298: 	if state.SchemaVersion != FlowStateSchemaVersion {
299: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: schemaVersion %d", ErrFlowStateUnsupported, path, state.SchemaVersion)
300: 	}
301: 	if state.Project == "" || state.Sprint == "" || state.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
302: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing required top-level fields", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
303: 	}
304: 	if state.Project != s.Project {
305: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: project mismatch %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Project)
306: 	}
307: 	if state.Sprint != s.Slug {
308: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: sprint mismatch %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Sprint)
309: 	}
310: 	if len(state.Stages) != len(PlanningStages()) {
311: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: expected %d stages", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, len(PlanningStages()))
312: 	}
313: 	seen := map[PlanningStage]bool{}
314: 	for i, stage := range state.Stages {
315: 		if stage.Stage != PlanningStages()[i] {
316: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %d is %q; expected %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, i, stage.Stage, PlanningStages()[i])
317: 		}
318: 		if !ValidStage(stage.Stage) {
319: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsupported stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
320: 		}
321: 		if seen[stage.Stage] {
322: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: duplicate stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
323: 		}
324: 		seen[stage.Stage] = true
325: 		if !ValidStatus(stage.Status) {
326: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsupported status %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, stage.Status)
327: 		}
328: 		if stage.Path == "" {
329: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %d missing path", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, i)
330: 		}
331: 		if filepath.IsAbs(stage.Path) || strings.HasPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(stage.Path))), "../") {
332: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe path", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
333: 		}
334: 		if _, err := resolveSprintContained(root, s, stage.Path); err != nil {
335: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe path: %w", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, err)
336: 		}
337: 		if strings.ContainsAny(stage.Error, "\x00\r\n") {
338: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsafe error detail", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage)
339: 		}
340: 		switch stage.LatestOutcome {
341: 		case "", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted", "cleanup_uncertain":
342: 		default:
343: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: stage %q has unsupported latest outcome %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, stage.Stage, stage.LatestOutcome)
344: 		}
345: 	}
346: 	for _, expected := range PlanningStages() {
347: 		if !seen[expected] {
348: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing stage %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, expected)
349: 		}
350: 	}
351: 	if state.Review != nil {
352: 		if err := validateReviewStageState(root, s, *state.Review, path); err != nil {
353: 			return err
354: 		}
355: 	}
356: 	if state.Smoke != nil {
357: 		if err := validateSmokeStageState(root, s, *state.Smoke, path); err != nil {
358: 			return err
359: 		}
360: 	}
361: 	if state.QA != nil {
362: 		if err := validateQAFlowSummary(root, s, *state.QA, path); err != nil {
363: 			return err
364: 		}
365: 	}
366: 	return nil
367: }

369: func validateQAFlowSummary(root string, s Sprint, summary QAFlowSummary, path string) error {
370: 	if !containsQAPhase(summary.Phase) || summary.CompletedShards < 0 || summary.TotalShards < 0 || summary.CompletedShards > summary.TotalShards || summary.Confirmed < 0 || summary.Blocked < 0 {
371: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid QA summary", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
372: 	}
373: 	if summary.StatePath == "" || !validFingerprint(summary.StateDigest) || strings.TrimSpace(summary.NextAction) == "" {
374: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: incomplete QA summary pointer", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
375: 	}
376: 	resolved, err := resolveSprintContained(root, s, summary.StatePath)
377: 	if err != nil || filepath.Base(resolved) != "state.json" || filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(resolved)) != "verification" {
378: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsafe QA summary pointer", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
379: 	}
380: 	if summary.CurrentAttemptID != "" && !validQAID(summary.CurrentAttemptID) {
381: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid QA summary attempt ID", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
382: 	}
383: 	return nil
384: }

386: func NewFlowState(s Sprint, stages []StageState, now time.Time) FlowState {
387: 	if now.IsZero() {
388: 		now = time.Now().UTC()
389: 	}
390: 	return FlowState{
391: 		SchemaVersion: FlowStateSchemaVersion,
392: 		Project:       s.Project,
393: 		Sprint:        s.Slug,
394: 		UpdatedAt:     now.UTC(),
395: 		Stages:        stages,
396: 	}
397: }

reasoning_details.text:
Very important discovery: **There is a DB-authoritative flow-state path** (`loadFlowStateDatabase` / `FlowStateInDatabase` / `saveFlowStateDatabase`). The context pack noted "no test drives the DB-authoritative branch interacting with review saves". Let me examine that code — this is a prime suspect for the failure/concurrency lens: two storage backends (DB + file mirror), and SaveFlowState writes DB then conditionally mirrors to the file. If Review saves go to DB while some readers read only the file, or if the file mirror is skipped for non-checkpoint states (`flowStateCheckpoint`) — look at line 225-228: ```go if authoritative, err := FlowStateInDatabase(root, s); err != nil { return err } else if authoritative { if err := saveFlowStateDatabase(root, s, state); err != nil { return err } if !flowStateCheckpoint(state) { return nil } return saveFlowStateWithHooks(root, s, state, atomicWriteHooks{}) } ``` So with a DB present, EVERY save writes the DB; the FILE gets updated ONLY when `flowStateCheckpoint(state)` is true — i.e., when ALL stages are complete/failed/skipped. During an active review run (stages not all terminal — e.g., execute complete but review/smoke stages... wait Stages here is planningStages list; after execute completes, are all planning stages complete? PlanningStages() probably includes requirements..plan; StageExecute is appended in flowStages but maybe not in PlanningStages. Let me check: `flowStages` does `ordered := append(PlanningStages(), StageExecute)`. So PlanningStages() = 7 planning stages. After execute, all 7 complete → flowStateCheckpoint true → file mirrored. During review running saves: state.Stages unchanged (all complete presumably since review happens post-execute) → checkpoint true → file written too. Hmm so during review, file IS updated on each save... IF all 7 planning stages terminal. But consider mid-planning review? Not possible (review requires execute). Wait, but there's something bigger here: **the resume/checkpoint semantics under DB-authoritative mode**. updateReviewResume → LoadFlowState (reads DB first), modifies, SaveFlowState (writes DB + file). Consistent. Now what about LoadFlowState reading DB and validating — ValidateFlowState(root, s, state, path) with `path` from FlowStatePath. Fine. Let me now find loadFlowStateDatabase/saveFlowStateDatabase/FlowStateInDatabase implementation. Where's the DB? Probably internal/platform or workspace-level SQLite ("durable operations"). Let me grep. Also key question for the failure lens: **`SaveFlowState` merge behavior**: if caller passes state WITHOUT Review/Smoke/QA, it loads prior and fills them in. Callers that DO pass Review replace wholesale. In saveReviewState, state loaded fresh then current replaced — fine. But notice: `saveReviewState` loads via LoadFlowState which prefers DB; then SaveFlowState writes DB + maybe file. OK. Now — **`state.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()`** in saveFlowStateWithHooks line 247: uses REAL clock, not s.now! Test determinism aside, fine. Next: the file lock `.ultraplan/locks/sprint/

--.lock` uses O_EXCL create + PID liveness check. Race window: process A creates lock, crashes WITHOUT releasing (kill -9). PID dead → next acquirer removes stale lock and retries. Two processes B and C both see stale lock simultaneously: both attempt os.Remove — one succeeds, other gets ErrNotExist tolerated (`removeErr != nil && !errors.Is(removeErr, fs.ErrNotExist)` → tolerate). Then BOTH proceed to attempt #2 O_EXCL create — one wins, other gets ErrExist again → loop ends (attempt<2) → returns conflict error. OK safe-ish. But subtle TOCTOU: A alive holding lock; B reads info, PID alive → conflict. Good. A releases between B's read and B's remove? B would remove A's FRESH lock? No wait: B only reaches Remove if verificationProcessAlive(existing.PID)==false. If A released, file gone → B's readErr → conflict error "unreadable lock". Hmm — actually if A released (removed file) before B reads: B's OpenFile O_EXCL succeeds (file absent) → B acquires. Fine. Race where B read info (A alive), A releases, C acquires, B removes C's fresh lock because stale-check passed on A's old info!! Sequence: 1. A holds lock (PID_A). 2. B: OpenFile → EEXIST; reads info (PID_A alive? suppose A just died → NOT alive) → decides stale. 3. A's release runs?? No—A died. Let me construct with live A: 1. A holds. 2. B opens → EEXIST → reads info PID_A. 3. A releases (removes file) legitimately finishing work. 4. C acquires (creates file, PID_C). 5. B checks PID_A — dead? No, A is alive (it just finished normally). Hmm for B to pass staleness, PID_A must be dead. If A is dead it can't have released (release requires live process)... unless PID reuse! PID_A dead, file still exists (crash). B reads (PID_A dead) → stale. Meanwhile ANOTHER process D also reads (PID_A dead) → stale. B removes file, D's remove gets ErrNotExist (tolerated). B creates → owner. D creates → EEXIST → reads B's info → PID_B alive → conflict error. Clean. PID reuse hazard: PID_A dead; OS reuses PID_A for unrelated process Q. Lock file from crashed A remains. B reads PID_A → kill(PID_A,0) succeeds because Q now has that PID → "pid alive" → B blocked FOREVER until Q dies. Liveness issue requiring manual intervention (rm lock). Realistic? PID reuse within the lifetime of an abandoned lock file — plausible on busy systems with high PID churn (Linux pid_max default 4M w/ rolling reuse; containers often 32768!). In a container with pid_max=32768, reuse is quick. Consequence: `sprint review` (and every mutation) fails with ErrVerificationConflict until unrelated PID exits. Severity: operational availability, medium-low; confidence medium (implementation-dependent). It's also pre-existing infrastructure shared by all stages — not review-specific. The gauntlet says report concrete failures; this is a real liveness defect but belongs to the locks surface shared across stages. I might note it as adjacent finding with clear scoping. Now — the BIG missing piece: DB-authoritative flow state. Let me find loadFlowStateDatabase etc.

reasoning_details.text:
Critical observation in `saveFlowStateDatabase`:

```go
header := state
header.Stages = nil
```

`header` is a COPY of FlowState with Stages=nil — but FlowState contains POINTER fields: `Review *ReviewStageState`, `Smoke *...`, `QA *...`. Those pointers are SHARED between header and state. json.Marshal(header) serializes Review/Smoke/QA from the same underlying data. Not a mutation issue here (no mutation after copy). OK.

Now the DB-authoritative path in SaveFlowState:
```go
if authoritative {
    saveFlowStateDatabase(...)
    if !flowStateCheckpoint(state) { return nil }
    return saveFlowStateWithHooks(...)  // file mirror
}
```

**Key failure-mode question: during a review run in DB-authoritative mode, are the per-completion resume saves mirrored to the file?** flowStateCheckpoint(state) checks ALL 7 planning stages terminal. Post-execute sprint: all planning stages complete → checkpoint TRUE → file mirror happens on every review save. Good.

But WAIT — what about the DB round-trip fidelity? loadFlowStateDatabase unmarshals Header into FlowState, then APPENDS stages from Items. Header includes Review/Resume/etc. Round-trip through JSON — time.Time precision: RFC3339 with nanoseconds? Go time.Time JSON marshal preserves nanoseconds. OK.

**BUT here's something:** `LoadFlowState` on the DB path validates via ValidateFlowState — which calls validateReviewStageState etc. Fine.

Now the deeper question for the review surface: **`updateReviewResume` and `saveReviewState` do Load→mutate→Save of the ENTIRE FlowState. In DB mode, productstate.Store.Save — is it transactional/atomic with respect to concurrent writers?** The mutation lease serializes reviews; but QA store, smoke, execute also write flow-state? Execute writes ExecuteRunState separately. Planning stage writers call SaveFlowState too (under lease). Status recompute (service.go) — does it SaveFlowState? Context pack said "Status-side Stale recomputation (service.go:266-295)". Let me check whether status writes happen WITHOUT the lease concurrently with review.

Also `productstate` package — check Store.Load/Save semantics (SQLite? files?). Let me look at internal/productstate.

Also I must check `verify.go` Verify(To=review) lines 51-81 and its "skip when current evidence exists" logic + assessment ladder, since flow --to review routes there.

And then review_test.go to see what's pinned. And app/sprint_commands.go durable op wiring.

Let me read service.go around status stale recompute, verify.go top, and productstate store.

reasoning_details.text:
**CONFIRMED RACE CANDIDATE — status writes vs active review:**

`Status` (service.go ~250-295) does:
1. `LoadFlowState` (line 250)
2. Recompute stages + Stale flags, keeping `refreshed.Review = state.Review`
3. **`SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, refreshed)` at line 292 WITHOUT holding the mutation lease.**

Meanwhile an active Review run is continuously doing Load→mutate→Save on flow-state.json (updateReviewResume per session event, saveReviewState per completion). Status's save writes back the ENTIRE FlowState including the Review record it loaded EARLIER.

Concrete bad outcome: 
1. T0: user runs `ultraplan sprint p s review` in terminal A. Fan-out starts; reviewer for contract X completes → flow-state records Resume checkpoint X=completed with result.
2. T1: user runs `sprint status` (or TUI/web polls status — operation runner likely calls Status periodically!) in terminal B. Status loads state at some point BEFORE X's completion save (or between load and save), recomputes, and saves the WHOLE state including the STALE Review record.
3. If status's Save lands AFTER review's X-completion save, X's completed checkpoint is REVERTED to running/stale-session.
4. Terminal A's review continues; suppose it crashes/is cancelled before X re-completes... actually X already produced its done item and won't be resent. On a later resume rerun, X reruns from scratch (continue-session). Wasted work but not corruption.
5. Worse variant: status's stale write lands BETWEEN review's final artifact write and final saveReviewState(completed)? Final save overwrites wholesale from ITS loaded state? No — final saveReviewState LOADS FRESH at that moment, so it picks up whatever's on disk plus its own mutations. The lost-update only matters if review's own load happens BEFORE the interleaved foreign save and its save AFTER. That's exactly the updateReviewResume window: Load→update→Save. A status save landing inside that window gets clobbered by review (status's changes lost — e.g., Stale recompute reverted) or vice versa clobbers review's checkpoint.

Also NOTE: `refreshed.Review.Stale` recomputation calls **`s.PrepareReview(...)`** (line 270) — a HEAVY full-manifest preparation — while review may be mid-run. PrepareReview is read-only though. But wait, worse: PrepareReview with persistCache? No — prepareSharedPromptContext is NOT called in PrepareReview... let me double check: PrepareReview doesn't call prepareSharedPromptContext (that happens in Review/PromptReview after). Right, PrepareReview only reads files. OK read-only.

So the race is real: concurrent `Status` (or any lease-free flow-state writer) can interleave read-modify-write with an active review's checkpoint persistence, losing resume progress or reverting stage states. Also two statuses racing each other.

256: 	if review.Fresh && review.Verdict == string(ReviewFail) {

260: 		return AssessmentBlocked, "Satisfy the review prerequisite and rerun review."
261: 	}
262: 	if !review.Fresh || review.ExecutionStatus != string(ReviewCompleted) || !smoke.Fresh || smoke.ExecutionStatus != string(SmokeCompleted) {
263: 		if !review.Fresh || review.ExecutionStatus != string(ReviewCompleted) {
264: 			return AssessmentIncomplete, "Run or retry review, the earliest non-current verification stage."
265: 		}
266: 		return AssessmentIncomplete, "Run or retry smoke, the earliest non-current verification stage."
267: 	}
268: 	switch SmokeVerdict(smoke.Verdict) {
269: 	case SmokeFailVerdict:
270: 		return AssessmentFail, "Resolve the classified failure and rerun the required containing suite."
271: 	case SmokeBlockedVerdict:
272: 		return AssessmentBlocked, "Restore smoke prerequisites, coverage, or evidence and rerun smoke."
273: 	case SmokeNotApplicable:

275: 	case SmokePassWithOpenIssues:
276: 		return AssessmentPassWithFindings, "Resolve linked relevant issues and rerun narrow plus containing scope."
277: 	case SmokePass:
278: 		if ReviewVerdict(review.Verdict) == ReviewPassWithFindings {
279: 			return AssessmentPassWithFindings, "Address review findings if a clean assessment is required."
280: 		}
281: 		return AssessmentPass, "No verification action required."

100: func (r *concurrentReviewRuntime) StartRun(_ context.Context, req pruntime.Request) (pruntime.Result, error) {
101: 	n := r.active.Add(1)
102: 	for {
103: 		old := r.max.Load()
104: 		if n <= old || r.max.CompareAndSwap(old, n) {
105: 			break
106: 		}
107: 	}
108: 	time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
109: 	r.active.Add(-1)
110: 	data, _ := json.Marshal(ReviewCoverageResult{SchemaVersion: 1, CoverageID: req.Metadata["coverage"], Applicability: "direct", Summary: "checked"})
111: 	return pruntime.Result{Events: []pruntime.Event{{Payload: map[string]any{"content": string(data)}}}, Permissions: pruntime.PermissionSummary{Mode: "restricted"}}, nil
112: }

reasoning_details.text:
Tests confirm the context pack. Now key hypotheses to verify/disprove:

**H-A (status-vs-review lost update)**: Confirmed structurally. Status writes flow-state lease-free at service.go:292 while Review holds the lease and does load-modify-save cycles. Let me also check TUI/web operation paths — do they poll Status during operations? Check app/operation_runner.go and web handlers.

**H-B (focus-mode clears ActiveAttempt+Resume then focus plan fails → prior resume destroyed)**: Look again: focus error path (review.go:464-469) — persistReviewFailure with result.Status=Blocked. saveReviewState: status != running → attempt terminal; Verdict restored from LastComplete if present. But Resume was ALREADY cleared by the first running save (line 461 + saveReviewState line 1227-1230). So a focus run that fails validation destroys the retained resume checkpoints AND their session IDs, even though nothing was rerun. Impact: interrupted full-run resume capability lost; sessions leak in runtime stores until sweep. Wait — but focus mode REQUIRES LastComplete with same fingerprint and valid retained coverage for every non-focused id. If LastComplete exists with valid coverage... then what was Resume tracking? An interrupted run AFTER a completion. E.g., run 1 completes fully (LastComplete set). Inputs change slightly? No—focus requires same fingerprint. Hmm: after completed review, Resume is nil anyway. So focus requires a state where LastComplete exists AND possibly Resume exists from an interrupted subsequent run with SAME fingerprint. Scenario: complete review (LastComplete). Then user runs review again (no restart): PrepareReview same fingerprint; running save: Restarted=false, Focused empty → ActiveAttempt kept/reused? current.ActiveAttempt nil (last run terminal) → new attempt; Resume nil → initializeReviewResume: state.Review.ActiveAttempt exists now; current=nil → rebuild all pending (rebased=0 since no prior resume)... wait — rebuild branch requires `restart || !reviewResumeCompatible(current=nil, m)` → rebuild; `!restart && reviewResumeShapeCompatible(nil,m)=false` → no prior map; all pending; rebased 0. Saved. Then reviewers start; interrupt after 1 coverage → Resume has 1 completed + sessions. NOW user runs --focus <other-id>: first running save CLEARS ActiveAttempt+Resume (Focused>0 condition). Then reviewCoveragePlan loads LastComplete — same fingerprint ✓ — non-focused ids must be in LastComplete.Coverage as valid. LastComplete.Coverage = results from the LAST COMPLETED review — which is complete (run 1). The interrupted run's extra completed checkpoint (say contract X re-validated) is LOST from resume but X IS in LastComplete already (from run 1) so focus proceeds. Focus completes → fine.

So the destruction only loses the interrupted run's partial progress BEYOND LastComplete. Since focus can only run when LastComplete covers everything valid, the loss is: (a) resumed-run completions not yet in LastComplete (they'd be recomputed later), (b) retained session continuity. Moderate waste, no correctness loss. AND it's arguably intended ("focused runs clear ActiveAttempt+Resume at this first running save" per context pack §2.2 step 6 — documented behavior). Not reporting as defect; maybe worth a note.

**H-C: `reviewCoveragePlan` uses LoadFlowState which prefers DB; but saveReviewState wrote to DB+file consistently. OK.
